title: Linux - Kernel/LPE/CVE Material (formerly Kernel/LPE/CVE material)
html:
Kernel, LPE, and CVE Material

These case studies cover distinct local privilege escalation primitives. Check the affected product or kernel, configuration, and prerequisites in each article before applying a technique. For broader host enumeration, use the Linux privilege escalation checklist.

For Dirty Pipe (CVE-2022-0847), the original research identifies upstream stable fixes at 5.10.102, 5.15.25, and 5.16.11. A kernel version in an older affected range is only a review lead: distribution kernels can backport fixes under different release names, and the relevant target file must be readable for the page-cache write primitive. Overwriting a readable SUID executable is one possible privilege path when its set-ID transition remains effective; modifying /etc/passwd and then authenticating can also depend on the local PAM stack. Check the installed vendor kernel package, running kernel after reboot, target permissions, mount nosuid, and no_new_privs before assessing reachability. Do not run a write probe during passive enumeration. See Ubuntu's release-specific status.

  • VMware Tools service discovery, CVE-2025-41244: privileged execution through untrusted process-path discovery.
  • AF_ALG splice page-cache overwrite, CVE-2026-31431: a kernel page-cache overwrite path.
  • POSIX CPU timers TOCTOU race and exploitation, CVE-2025-38352: timer expiry/deletion under task exit, including IRQ-path prerequisites and exploit research.
  • Linux ptrace exit race and pidfd_getfd file-descriptor theft: descriptor access across a process exit race.

Related binary exploitation case studies

The Binary Exploitation section goes deeper into exploit primitives, memory layout, and mitigation bypasses for these Linux kernel targets:

  • AF_UNIX out-of-band SKB use-after-free: a socket bug developed into kernel read and write primitives.
  • AF_ALG concurrent-writer scatterlist underflow: a skcipher writer race developed into a kernel write.
  • Futex PI use-after-free: a pointer-write primitive extended through pipe buffers and workqueues.
  • ksmbd streams out-of-bounds write, CVE-2025-37947: kernel heap exploitation and mitigation bypasses.
  • Arm64 static linear-map KASLR bypass: address discovery for arm64 kernel exploitation.
  • Adreno A7xx GPU/SMMU privilege bypass: an Android GPU path to kernel memory access.
  • Pixel Bigwave job-timeout use-after-free: an Android accelerator bug used for kernel writes.
